earlier_scan.source_named: Read Lebold, Kriens & Susanto 2013 SIL survey ( via the Internet Archive): wordlist survey, no stress statement; no grammar of Kia River Awyu exists

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco. 2016. Aghu: Annotated texts with grammatical introduction and vocabulary lists (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 33). Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Aghu only (neighbouring Awyu language, aghu1255): sec. 1.2.3 'Lexical stress is on the last syllable of the word. Drabbe speaks of a "weak accent."' Discusses the exonym 'Djair' as an outsiders' name for the Aghu. Not a source for Kia River/Jair Awyu [awv].

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1968. The Central and South New Guinea Phylum: a report on the language situation in south New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 8 (Pacific Linguistics A-16), 1-17. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing: zero occurrences of stress / accent / tone / tonal / pitch / suprasegmental in the whole text; the Awyu section gives only Drabbe's dialect list and cognation percentages (e.g. Syiagha-Yenimu 84%, Kaeti-Syiagha 31%).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and JSON for jair1235 'Kia River Awyu' [awv]
sources.note: Catalogue record only: zero grammar/phonology/sketch references; refs are Lebold et al. 2013, van den Heuvel & Fedden 2014, Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Wichmann, Soren, Eric W. Holman, Cecil H. Brown, Matthew S. Dryer & Qibin Ran (eds). 2025. The ASJP Database (version 21): doculect JAIR_AWYU (awv / jair1235; transcriber M. S. Dryer; ASJP source 3776 = Lebold, Kriens & Susanto 2013). 74 forms.
sources.note: nothing: 40-/100-item ASJP list re-keyed from Lebold, Kriens & Susanto 2013's Ujung Kia Jair Awyu column without stress marks

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [last modified 2024-06-25]. 'Awyu' and 'Southeast Awyu' (with stub subpages 'Lower Kia River Awyu', 'Upper Kia River Awyu'). New Guinea World (online comparative database), University of Zurich hosting.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Segmental historical phonology only (vowel fronting, lenition of medial voiced stops in Southeast Awyu, palatalization of *t complete in Lower Kia River and partial in Upper Kia River); no word on stress, accent or tone. Source list confirms no data source for the Kia River lects beyond Lebold et al. 2013.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2020. The Greater Awyu Languages of West Papua. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Nothing on Jair/Kia River Awyu; ch. 2 phonology treats only Aghu ('Word stress is a weak accent on the last syllable of words', p. 10), Digul Wambon ('Stress is a weak accent on the penultimate syllable', p. 11), Kombai and Korowai (contrastive pitch accent). p. 4: 'Aghu (Axu, also known as Jair)' -- Drabbe's 'Djair' is the Aghu (aghu1255), not Ethnologue's Jair Awyu [awv]. p. ~166 quotes Susanto (2004: 16) on Jair (Awyu) speakers at Boma II, sociolinguistic only.

sources.citation: Wester, Ruth. 2014. A linguistic history of Awyu-Dumut: morphological study and reconstruction of a Papuan language family. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
sources.note: Nothing on Jair/Kia River Awyu. Sec. 1.1.14 (pp. 9-10): the SIL surveys (Jang 2003, Susanto 2004, Hughes 2009, Kriens & Lebold 2010, Kriens et al. 2013) 'do not contain any morphological data and are hence not a source of data'; she limits herself to the languages described by Drabbe and de Vries (Shiaxa, Yenimu, Pisa, Aghu, Mandobo, Yonggom/Digul Wambon, Kombai). Stress mentioned only for noun compounds (first noun stressed, grave accent).

sources.citation: Lebold, Randy, Ronald Kriens & Yunita Susanto. 2013. A report on the Bamgi, Kia, and Lower Digul River language survey in Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-008. 52 pp.
sources.note: Nothing stated. Sociolinguistic/lexicostatistic survey with no phonology section. Appendix H (pp. 36-48) prints the only published Jair Awyu data, a 239-item IPA wordlist from Ujung Kia with primary-stress marks (e.g. 001 'head' ˈxabaŋ, 004 'ear' tiˈto, 011 'elbow' ˈbəɾamukɔ); Appendix I a 50-item list from Subur. My script tally of the marks in that column (approximate): of 145 polysyllabic tokens with a mark, 119 first-syllable, 22 final (21 of them disyllables), 4 penult in trisyllables -- transcription data, not a claim by the authors. sources.citation: Susanto, Yunita. 2005. Report on the Edera District survey, south coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2005-025.
sources.note: Nothing; survey (Pies and Memes later assigned to Jair Awyu per Lebold et al. 2013 fn. 20); no wordlists printed, only 'accents.. are ignored' in the lexical-similarity rules.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1950. Twee dialecten van de Awju-taal. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 106: 92-147.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Shiaxa/Yenimu (and Pisa), i.e. South Awyu/Asue Awyu, not this variety: p. 96 'De toon, die op een syllabe valt, lijkt veel op de Nederlandse klemtoon; we geven hem aan met een accent-grave' -- stress exists and is marked per word, no placement rule.

sources.note: Not this variety (Aghu, aghu1255), but the nearest fully described Awyu language; its final-syllable 'weak accent' statement is the only family-internal placement rule and would be the proxy if the catalog ever admits sister-language inference (it should not be entered under jair1235).
